newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese teachers on one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese teachers on one-day strike.

text.p: Lebanon's 70,000 schoolteachers went on a one-day strike on Thursday to press the government to pay them overdue salary increases.
Newspapers said up to one million students were affected by the strike.
"The strike is perfect, all schools have stopped," teachers' union spokesman Hanna Gharib told Reuters.
"We want our salaries to be paid on the basis of the new pay scales that were adopted in July by the government and parliament," he said.

The new rates agreed by the government should have been paid to the teachers immediately after parliament approved them in July, but the government has not included funds for the increase in the state budget.
Officials told Reuters on Thursday that the law increasing the teachers' pay scales contained a technical error and it must be resubmitted to parliament.
The new rates would cost the cash-strapped government 300 billion Lebanese pounds ($189 million) a year, according to Beirut newspapers.
Gharib said the strike was just the first of a series that teachers' unions are preparing to press their demands.
"Today's strike is just a first step...it will be followed by four-day strike on December 4, 5, 6 and 7, then an open ended strike in the first half of January," he added.
